newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain futures settlement seen causing bourse havoc.
newsitem.headline: Spain futures settlement seen causing bourse havoc.

text.p: Unusually high open interest of more than 20,000 contracts for June IBEX futures may cause havoc on the bourse later today after the expiry.

Dealers were split on which direction the market would go during the "witching hour", the calculation period for settlements between 1415 GMT and 1445 GMT, but many dealers expected high volatility and volume.
"It will be madness, with large trades and crossed positions", said a dealer.
The likely trend of the market is bullish and the futures contract will probably remain above 6.700 points, said Rolf Muller at BZW in Madrid.
"The market appears to be on the road to new highs once again...Yesterday we had foreign cash coming in and the Ibex did not reach a new record though the Madrid stock market index did.

"That seems to indicate that smaller stocks are adjusting and that the market is less focused on blue chips. In any case, I think the pressure during settlement time will be on the buy side and we'll certainly close somewhere above 6,700 points," Muller said.
Other dealers agreed, saying the large open interest pointed to an active settlement.

"We will have to see how arbitrage goes this afternoon, but settlement could be busy. There has been quite a bit of direct arbitrage and the spread is expensive, so we could see action on both the buy and sell side," said Alberto Carrasco of Benito y Monjardin.
Juan Perez, of Inverban brokerage, shared the view of other dealers that the settlement will be active due to the large open interest and the jump in the roll-over cost.

"The open interest is very high compared to other months and the roll-over has surged, so those with baskets will find it difficult. It would not be strange if some opted to let their positions expire and then compensated their positions in baskets," he said.

The transfer of positions to the following settlement has become expensive over the last few days and has forced some players to keep the current settlement in their portfolios to avoid paying a surcharge for the roll-over.
For this reason, and because of some financial products linked to the average Ibex and to today's settlement, dealers expected these strong movements.

"Open interest is high for a settlement day (over 20,000 contracts). This could largely be explained by a more expensive roll-over in the last few days," said Muller. "Over the last two days we have seen a change in attitude regarding the market, with fresh cash coming in and people preferring to play with July or later settlements."
In Muller and other dealer's opinion, besides the high open interest, settlement linked products could affect business today.
"There are several financial products (warrants, funds, bonds) which take their references from today's settlement or from the average price and that could condition today's business", a dealer said.
Special situations which affect the Ibex-35, published by the Madrid Stock Market Bulletin, include six products linked to the Ibex average or to today's settlement.
Regarding today's large open interest, dealers believe that the higher roll-over cost could force some into allowing their positions to expire.
"There are over 20,000 open contracts, which is inusual for a settlement day", said Alberto Carrasco. "The roll-over has been expensive and I believe some positions will be allowed to expire".
